hooks.command: s="$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/protect-env.sh"; if [ -f "$s" ]; then exec "$s"; fi; git -C "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" cat-file -e HEAD:.claude/hooks/protect-env.sh 2>/dev/null && exit 2; exit 0
s="$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/lint-check.sh"; if [ -f "$s" ]; then exec "$s"; fi; git -C "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" cat-file -e HEAD:.claude/hooks/lint-check.sh 2>/dev/null && exit 2; exit 0

hooks.prompt: This session is about to be compacted. Read the transcript and decide whether it surfaced a reusable convention, gotcha or pattern that is not already written down in CLAUDE.md, a rule or a skill. Answer {"ok": true} if there is nothing new. Otherwise answer {"ok": false, "reason": "<the lesson, and where it belongs: a path-scoped rule under .claude/rules/ or a skill>"} — the reason is surfaced to Claude, which can then write it down before the context that learned it is gone.
